summary: Dependabot bump of the monitoring Prometheus image from v3.15.1 to v3.16.0 in monitoring/compose.yaml; only the tag and its digest change. The digest sha256:e04987641b57704f408e31f6373ba4138ecf27cb4a165d24aabb6c38fddd0f06 equals the current multi-arch index digest of prom/prometheus:v3.16.0 on Docker Hub, so the reference stays immutable (ADR-0055). Compose bumps are outside the narrow Dependabot exemption of ADR-0050, hence this record. Read the v3.16.0 release notes (published 2026-11-05): the [CHANGE] entries concern experimental search endpoints, --web.external-url defaulting to https only with --web.config.file TLS (not used here), PromQL sample statistics, deprecated remote-write 2.0 metadata metrics, remote-write receiver counting and exemplar label uniqueness; none affects this stack's flags (config.file, tsdb.path, web.listen-address, web.enable-lifecycle), its scrape configuration or the storage.tsdb.retention block. User 65534, the loopback port binding, volumes and secrets are unchanged. No new trust boundary, port, credential or network destination.

findings.evidence: A third-party container image is updated; a compromised release would run with the stack's metrics credentials.
findings.resolution: Pre-existing and unchanged in scope: the image stays pinned by digest (verified against the registry), runs as nobody with the port bound to loopback; release notes reviewed.

tests.command: Docker Hub registry HEAD /v2/prom/prometheus/manifests/v3.16.0 (index media types)
tests.evidence: Docker-Content-Digest sha256:e04987641b57704f408e31f6373ba4138ecf27cb4a165d24aabb6c38fddd0f06, identical to the pinned digest.

limitations: The image was not started; deploy_ct.py checks health, scrape target and the first data point when it rolls out.
v3.16.0 was published on 2026-11-05; the operator's 7-day minimum image age is reached on 2026-11-12.
